answer: Because the summit ledger attributes every share, the sonnet audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 44% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it pays the atlas fee twice and still divides one payout. The fee repeats 27 times over. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
